content: A pinguecula is a form of conjunctival degeneration that occurs in the eye. It is a very common condition and is characterized by the presence of a yellow-white deposit on the conjunctiva, located near the limbus, which is the anatomical junction between the cornea and the sclera. Clinically, it is important to differentiate a pinguecula from a pterygium, as the latter is a wedge-shaped area of fibrosis that appears to invade the cornea. From a histological perspective, a pinguecula is marked by degeneration of the collagen fibers within the conjunctival stroma, thinning of the overlying epithelial layer, and occasional calcification. Although a pinguecula may slowly increase in size over time, it is a benign condition that typically does not require medical or surgical intervention. However, in cases where cosmetic concerns arise, surgical excision may be performed. Additionally, a pinguecula is considered one of the differential diagnoses when evaluating a limbal nodule.
